read me first · ≈ 7 minutes

Before the Ball

❦

Коротко о том, что мы учим в этом уроке, когда это ставить и как это звучит. Прочитай один раз до заданий и возвращайся сюда, если что-то забудешь. Все новые слова урока с переводом собраны внизу, в Glossary.

1. have something done
have+что+V3

Глагол have + предмет + третья форма глагола (past participle: made, cut, done, altered…).

Что значит и когда ставить

① Кто-то делает это для тебя. Ты не делаешь сама, а заказываешь услугу: стрижку, маникюр, пошив, ремонт, чистку, фото.

  • I had my dress made in Paris.Мне сшили платье в Париже (я заказала).
  • She has her nails done every Friday.Ей делают маникюр каждую пятницу.

② С тобой случилось что-то неприятное. Это никто не заказывал, просто так вышло.

  • The Duchess had her fan stolen.У герцогини украли веер.

Сравни

  • I cut my hair.Я подстриглась сама.
  • I had my hair cut.Меня подстригли в салоне.

Порядок слов

Предмет стоит между have и V3: I had my coat cleaned, а не I had cleaned my coat. Последнее означает совсем другое: «я (уже) почистила пальто сама».

2. Во всех временах

Меняется только have, остальное стоит на месте.

сейчас, обычноI have my hair cut every month.
сейчас, в процессеWe are having the curtains cleaned.
в прошломShe had her gown made.
уже сделаноI've had it altered twice.
в будущемI will (1774: shall) have my hair dressed.
с must / shouldYou should have your shoes mended.

Вопрос и отрицание: через do / does / did

  • Did you have it made?Тебе это сшили?
  • I don't have my nails done.Я не делаю маникюр в салоне.

get something done

То же самое, только разговорнее: I must get my shoes mended. В письме 1774 года так не пишут, а в чате с подругой — пожалуйста.

3. Как это звучит

have / had здесь звучит полностью, не сокращается: /hæv/, /hæd/. В have something done это смысловой глагол, а не вспомогательный.

  • I had my hair done./aɪ hæd maɪ ˈheə ˈdʌn/
  • I've had it altered./aɪv hæd ɪt ˈɔːltəd/первое ’ve — короткое вспомогательное, had — полное

Ударение падает на предмет и на V3, а не на have: I had my HAIR CUT.

Окончание -ed у V3 читается тремя способами:

  • /t/ dressed, washed, fixed
  • /d/ altered, cleaned, dyed
  • /ɪd/ painted, mended, decorated
4. Порядок прилагательных

Когда прилагательных несколько, они идут в таком порядке:

мнениеразмервозрастформацветоткудаиз чегоПРЕДМЕТ
  • a beautiful long pale-blue French silk gownмнение → размер → цвет → откуда → из чего
  • a small round marble tableразмер → форма → материал

and ставим только между двумя цветами: a pink and white fan, но a long and white gown → a long white gown.

Язык 1774 года

Письмо Софи написано так, как писали при дворе: shall вместо will, I pray you вместо please, a fortnight вместо two weeks. Это для настроения. Как сказать то же самое сегодня, разберём в разделе Then & Now.

≈ 12 minutes

A Letter from Versailles

❦

June 1774. The young Marie-Antoinette has just become Queen, and Sophie, seventeen, writes to her friend in the country. Guess the highlighted phrases from context first — then tap to check.

Versailles, the 3rd of June, 1774
My dearest Charlotte,

I pray you forgive my silence of a whole — I have scarcely had a moment to myself since we arrived at court. You cannot imagine the bustle! Everyone here is from morning till night, and a lady who appears with hair is talked about for a week.

On Saturday there is to be a great ball, and I am all impatience. Mama has had my gown made by Mademoiselle Bertin herself, the Queen's own dressmaker. It is a magnificent pale-blue silk gown, so that it slides through one's fingers, with sleeves of the finest lace. The bodice was a little too tight, so I have had it altered twice. On the morning of the ball I shall have my hair dressed and powdered — it takes three hours, and one cannot lean back for fear of ruining it!

You asked me to describe the people here. Imagine a in a coat of crimson cloth, then a young officer whose arms are too long for his sleeves. The Duchess of R. has a perfect , an and the palest I have ever seen — though I suspect her powder, which has a , helps a great deal. Her daughter to her, except for her hair, which she wears and simple, without powder. How brave!

I must confess one . At the opera last Tuesday, the Duchess had her fan stolen — a fan painted by a famous artist — and for a moment everyone looked at me, for I was sitting beside her! Happily, it was found under a chair, and the evening after that.

My only sorrow is my travelling cloak of grey wool, which looks very poor beside all this silk. I shall have a new one made before winter.

Write to me soon, and tell me everything.

I remain, dearest Charlotte,
your most affectionate friend,Sophie
the young QueenÉ. Vigée Le Brun, “Marie-Antoinette with a Rose”, 1783
True or false?
Sophie wrote to Charlotte every day.
Her gown was made by the Queen's dressmaker.
Sophie will powder her hair herself.
The Duchess's fan was found.
Show answers
  1. Sophie wrote to Charlotte every day. — False (she was silent for a fortnight)
  2. Her gown was made by the Queen's dressmaker. — True
  3. Sophie will powder her hair herself. — False (she will have it dressed and powdered)
  4. The Duchess's fan was found. — True
Answer, then check
1. Why hasn't Sophie written for two weeks?
Show answer
Life at court is so busy that she has scarcely had a moment to herself.
2. What has been done to her gown so far?
Show answer
It was made by Mademoiselle Bertin, and the bodice has been altered twice.
3. Why did everyone look at Sophie at the opera?
Show answer
The Duchess had her fan stolen, and Sophie was sitting beside her.
4. What will she have made before winter, and why?
Show answer
A new cloak — her coarse grey wool one looks poor beside all the silk.

≈ 15 minutes

Grammar

❦

have something done · the order of adjectives. Sophie uses both in every letter. Work them out yourself first, then open the rule.

from Sophie's letter
  1. Mama has had my gown made by Mademoiselle Bertin.
  2. I shall have my hair dressed and powdered.
  3. The Duchess had her fan stolen at the opera.
  4. a magnificent pale-blue silk gown
Sentence 1: who made the gown — Mama or Mademoiselle Bertin?
Check
Mademoiselle Bertin. Mama only arranged it: have + object + past participle.
Will Sophie dress her own hair?
Check
No — a hairdresser will; she arranges it. (shall = an old-fashioned will.)
Sentence 3: did the Duchess arrange this?
Check
Of course not! Here have something done means something bad happened to her: her fan was stolen.
Why magnificent pale-blue silk and not silk pale-blue magnificent?
Check
Opinion comes first, then colour, then material.

2. have / get something done

Use the words in brackets in the right form. Contractions are fine.

1. Last spring the Queen (have / her portrait / paint) by Madame Vigée Le Brun.
2. How often (you / have / your hair / powder)?
3. My gown is too long. I must (have / it / shorten).
4. We (have / the ballroom / decorate) at the moment, so there is no dancing.
5. The Count (have / his carriage / rob) on the road to Paris last week.
6. Your shoes are worn out. You should (get / them / mend).
7. Have you ever (have / your silhouette / cut)?
8. She looks different — I think she (have / her hair / curl).
Show answers
  1. had her portrait painted
  2. do you have your hair powdered
  3. have it shortened (or get)
  4. are having the ballroom decorated
  5. had his carriage robbed
  6. get them mended (or have)
  7. had your silhouette cut
  8. has had her hair curled (or had)

Then & Now

❦

Sophie writes the English of 1774. It is charming in a letter — and very strange in a modern email! Find the modern way to say each phrase.

Then → now

Say it the modern way. Tap the words in order — each one jumps into the line. One word in every set is extra. Tap a word in the line to send it back, then open the answers.

I pray you, be seated.
Pleasedown.praysit
I have not seen you this fortnight.
haven'tweeks.twoIsinceseenforyou
I am much obliged to you.
obligedmuch!Thankveryyou
I am all impatience for the ball.
thepatientwaitIcan'tforball!
What a vexing predicament!
situation!funnystickyaWhat
I must make my toilette.
toiletneedgetItoready.
Pray, tell me everything.
praytellmeSo,everything!
Your most humble servant, Sophie
BestservantSophiewishes,
Show answers
  1. I pray you, be seated. → Please sit down.
  2. I have not seen you this fortnight. → I haven't seen you for two weeks.
  3. I am much obliged to you. → Thank you very much!
  4. I am all impatience for the ball. → I can't wait for the ball!
  5. What a vexing predicament! → What a sticky situation!
  6. I must make my toilette. → I need to get ready.
  7. Pray, tell me everything. → So, tell me everything!
  8. Your most humble servant, Sophie → Best wishes, Sophie

One word in each set is extra: a toilet is a WC, not a toilette!

a word of advice

Use these phrases in your reply to Sophie — two or three of them will make your letter sound wonderfully old. In a real email to a friend today, use the modern ones.

One survivor: a fortnight is still perfectly normal in British English — “I'm going to Italy for a fortnight.”
